audit.issue: Wrong unit: revenue and market cap about 1,000 times too large for some firms
audit.detected_by: Carbon, water and energy scale with revenue within an industry; these firms sit about 1,000x below that relation
audit.treatment: Divide Revenue and Market_Cap by 1,000 for every row of the flagged firms
audit.effect: Mean market cap 213,205 -> 14,108 USD million; share of the 100 largest firm-years held by these firms 100% -> 0%

audit.issue: Near-duplicate monthly returns (two rows per company-month, values differ by at most 0.01)
audit.detected_by: Duplicate (Company_ID, Month) keys; no exact duplicates
audit.treatment: Keep the first row per company-month
audit.effect: Firm-years with a full 12 holding months 9,002 -> 9,182 (181 firm-years had 13 months and were dropped)

audit.issue: Analyst_Outlook behaves as if stamped with future information (related to the next 12-month return)
audit.detected_by: Rank correlation with the return in three 12-month windows: only the next window is non-zero
audit.treatment: Exclude from every model; listed in the feature table as excluded
audit.effect: Rank correlation with the next 12-month return 0.68 (other windows -0.01, 0.01); random forest test RMSE 37.59 without vs 29.14 with it (baseline 37.20)

audit.detected_by: 987 firms in the file vs 1,376 in the panel; 389 firms have a last fiscal year before 2025
audit.treatment: Build every sample and the benchmark on the full panel and hold exiting firms until their last month in the backtest (model fitting needs the full 12 months)
audit.effect: Equal-weight benchmark: 4.62% a year on the full panel vs 5.18% on survivors only (Sharpe 0.213 vs 0.248); the model samples also drop 302 firm-years of exiting firms (fewer than 12 holding months), plus 926 rows of formation year 2025 with only 6 months of returns

audit.issue: Restated scores behave as if they contain hindsight (not point-in-time)
audit.detected_by: Compared with the point-in-time scores; the changes correlate with later returns (inference: hindsight)
audit.treatment: Use the point-in-time scores everywhere; use the restated file only for the comparison in task (c)
audit.effect: 459 firms have every score changed (mean 5.7 points); within-year rank correlation of the Environmental score with the next excess return 0.010 (point-in-time) vs 0.056 (restated); 14% of the top-decile names change

audit.issue: Carbon, water and energy missing together, not at random
audit.detected_by: Missing share by region and by Environmental score
audit.treatment: Keep all rows; carbon intensity filled with the industry-year median plus a missing flag; raw water and energy not used
audit.effect: 13.2% of formation rows; Europe 6.3% vs 13.0% to 18.9% elsewhere; mean Environmental score 47.2 (missing) vs 56.5; dropping the carbon features changes the linear test RMSE 38.10 -> 38.05; dropping the rows with gaps would lose 13.2% of the sample and lift its mean Environmental score 55.3 -> 56.5

audit.issue: Values at the bounds: scores of exactly 0 or 100 (censoring) and monthly returns of exactly -95%
audit.detected_by: Counts of values at the minimum and maximum, for all three score components and in the restated file
audit.treatment: Kept and documented; cannot be told apart from real values
audit.effect: Environmental 65, Social 72, Governance 77 scores at 0 or 100 (213 panel rows, 1.5%, have at least one), 8 returns at -95%; removing the 94 training rows with a clipped score changes the linear test RMSE 38.10 -> 38.00

task_b.target: twelve-month total holding return in percent (July to June after formation)

task_c.conclusion: An investor could have earned an ESG premium only in firms in Europe, from 2021 (+3.1 points of 12-month excess return per standard deviation of the Environmental score; Holm-adjusted p = 0.018 with errors clustered by company, but p = 0.09 with its 4 formation years as the unit); no other region or period is distinguishable from zero, so this is a plausible, not a proven, premium, and it is a cross-sectional association, not a return shown to be tradable after costs.

bootstrap.statistic: Sharpe ratio difference, Linear regression (selected), floor 80th pct minus equal-weight benchmark; 84 months resampled with replacement, 5,000 draws, seed 12345, 95% percentile interval

task_d.universe: full panel including firms that left
